correctness.rationale: At critical aligned Zipf weights, the deterministic mean discovered mass is S_N(A)/H_N, with S_N(A)=sum_i(1-e^-A/i)/i. Splitting the infinite harmonic sum and subtracting i>N gives S_N(A)=log A+2gamma-A/N+O(1/A+A/N^2+A^2/N^2). Consequently its exact root is A_N=c_theta N^theta+c_theta^2 N^(2theta-1)+O_theta(1+N^(3theta-2)). The variance of the unnormalized discovered sum satisfies A V_N(A)->1/2 and A S_N'(A)->1; the triangular-array Lindeberg bound comes from isolating i<=A^(2/3), which are discovered with overwhelming probability, while all remaining scaled summands vanish. Threshold-event inversion yields (T_N/H_N-A_N)/sqrt(A_N)=>N(0,1/2), and replacing the exact root by first-order centering creates the theta=2/3 transition. Independent high-precision finite sums and root finding for N=5000,20000,80000 and theta=1/2,2/3,0.8 checked slope and variance convergence and the positive second correction.
